groups.title: Dark spells
groups.description: Scourge and the darker spell family. Compare a compact magical gesture with a longer creature-like texture; prioritize a readable attack when spells overlap.

candidates.role: Try for Scourge cast or blast
candidates.listen: Listen for a distinct magical attack that remains readable when repeated. Check whether it feels too synthetic.

candidates.role: Try for a contrasting dark spell cast
candidates.listen: Compare its onset and tail with the first option. Does it give a spell its own identity?

candidates.role: Texture for a major blast or dangerous windup
candidates.listen: Listen for a usable short portion. A creature-like sound may add menace, but reject it if it sounds like a character voice.

groups.title: Arcane force
groups.description: Gravity, Warp Zone, and magical impacts. These are promising areas to explore because their current character comes mainly from synthesis.

candidates.role: Try for a short warp or gravity transition
candidates.listen: Check whether the effect communicates displacement quickly. Reject an overtly retro or cartoon character if it clashes with the arena.

candidates.role: Try as the impact layer of a force spell
candidates.listen: Look for weight and a clear attack. Would it help distinguish a magical hit from a physical collision?

candidates.role: Try for a magical projectile impact
candidates.listen: Listen for a compact impact with enough character to recognize during a crowded fight.

groups.title: Teleport and swap
groups.description: Short position changes need a precise, recognizable gesture. Decide how organic or technological these spells should sound.

candidates.role: Try for teleport departure or arrival
candidates.listen: Compare its short timing with the current teleport. Does it communicate the movement without lingering?

candidates.role: Try for Swap or a more substantial teleport
candidates.listen: Check the full gesture and whether a shorter portion could work. Listen for an unwanted science-fiction character.

candidates.role: Try for an organic teleport accent
candidates.listen: Does the slurp-like character feel like dangerous magic, or does it become comic? That distinction matters here.

groups.title: Shield and reflection
groups.description: Explore a stable magical barrier, an impact, and a brighter spell accent. The final shield needs to read separately from teleport and damage effects.

candidates.role: Try as a subtle shield or barrier layer
candidates.listen: Judge the sustained character rather than the loop seam. Is it convincing magic, and would it remain tolerable while a shield is held?

candidates.role: Try a short portion for shield impact or reflection
candidates.listen: Listen for a useful impact inside the longer recording. Pass if it reads as machinery or futuristic weaponry.

candidates.role: Try for shield activation
candidates.listen: Compare its magical accent with the current shield. It should signal protection without resembling a reward jingle.

groups.title: Ice and snowball
groups.description: The current burst combines ice recordings with synthesis. Compare that physical crack against purpose-made magical ice effects.

candidates.role: Try for Snowball cast
candidates.listen: Check whether its short gesture has an identifiable cold character, rather than a generic spell sound.

candidates.role: Try for a fuller icy cast or burst
candidates.listen: Listen for a useful attack and tail. Would the longer effect become cluttered when several players cast?

candidates.role: Try for Snowball launch or a compact burst
candidates.listen: Compare its weight and clarity with the existing snow burst. Keep only the character you prefer.

groups.title: Fire and big impacts
groups.description: Two current references: the frequent Fireball cast and the heavier Meteor impact. Candidates can supply a new launch character, fire texture, or an accent for a major hit.

candidates.role: Try as a Fireball cast variation
candidates.listen: Compare this alternate take with our existing Fireball sound. Judge its repeated whoosh, not just the first impression.

candidates.role: Fire texture for a cast, ignition, or windup
candidates.listen: Listen for a useful section of magical fire. Check whether the recording has too much lead-in for a responsive spell.

candidates.role: Try as a Meteor or major magical explosion layer
candidates.listen: Judge the impact character separately from loudness. Is the tail short enough to coexist with the next spell?

groups.title: Lightning and electricity
groups.description: Lightning needs an immediate attack; sustained electrical texture belongs on held effects. Compare these against the current beam zap.

candidates.role: Electrical texture for Lightning or Link
candidates.listen: Look for a decisive usable transient or sustained texture. Pass if it sounds like a human vocal reaction.

candidates.role: Try for a compact zap or Bouncer hit
candidates.listen: Does it have a clear electrical identity without a playful laser-gun character?

candidates.role: Try as a short Lightning hit layer
candidates.listen: Listen for a crisp attack that will cut through the arena without becoming sharp or tiring.

groups.title: Stone and arena
groups.description: Physical material for Rockpillar, broken obstacles and collapsing arena tiles. The strongest candidates may supply small fragments for a layered effect.

candidates.role: Try as a stone impact or pillar debris layer
candidates.listen: Check the material weight and whether the sound reads as stone at game scale.

candidates.role: Try for a heavier stone impact
candidates.listen: Compare the attack and decay with the brick recording. A long natural tail may need a shorter edit.

candidates.role: Source material for obstacle break or arena collapse
candidates.listen: This longer recording is for choosing individual impacts and debris textures. Note a timestamp if a particular moment works.

groups.title: Shop purchases
groups.description: Explore physical coin sounds as a small material layer for buying spells. Compare them with the current complete purchase sound; a liked source would still need timing and mix work.

candidates.role: Try as a compact purchase accent
candidates.listen: Would a physical coin accent suit the spell shop? Keep it restrained enough for several quick purchases.

candidates.role: Try as a very short purchase or upgrade accent
candidates.listen: Check whether the transient is satisfying on its own or would need a quieter magical layer.

candidates.role: Coin texture for a major purchase or reward
candidates.listen: Listen for a shorter useful portion. Note whether the material feels substantial or too fussy for the shop.
